units.passage: This is the paradox of genAI—using it may actually appear to increase the quality of your work while simultaneously decreasing your actual learning
units.why: "using it may actually appear to increase the quality of your work while simultaneously decreasing your actual learning": false sense of mastery, P43.

units.passage: Be aware that students may think GenAI was only giving a hint or a little help whereas it is actually solving a key part of the problem. This is especially true for weaker students who may not recognize the difference.
units.why: Students 'may think GenAI was only giving a hint' when it solves a key part, especially weaker students; a false sense of what they did or mastered: P43.

units.passage: If AI was used, one should also submit a chatlog. Further guidance provided in class Should you use an AI tool to help you do your homework? You will have the ability to evaluate the output only really if you try to do it yourself first and gain that experience. While AI use is not prohibited in this course, you will be expected to understand the code that you submit to get full credit on the assignment. You need to understand the code to also do well on the exams. Before you use the internet/gen AI Try to do the assignment first with basic concepts and learning from errors. Use internet/generative AI to figure out errors only if you need it Acknowledge that what you used in the header comments of your code Make sure you understand what you have used from these outside sources.
units.why: ME 208: 'You need to understand the code to also do well on the exams' warns that unearned code shows on exams, P43.
units.fit_note: Says understanding is needed for exams; does not mention a false sense of mastery.

units.passage: They can also provide a false sense of security or ease as users handover their own critical and creative faculties to computers.
units.why: Warns tools "can also provide a false sense of security or ease as users handover their own critical and creative faculties"; reliance on AI gives false confidence and cedes thinking, P43.
units.fit_note: Says false sense of security or ease and handing over critical faculties, not mastery exposed on exams. / Concerns false security and surrendering critical faculties generally, not mastery exposed on exams.

units.passage: Getting the right answer from a chatbot can create the illusion of learning – but it can also trigger “cognitive surrender”4, where students fall back on AI at the first hint of struggle.
units.why: 'Getting the right answer from a chatbot can create the illusion of learning' is the false-sense-of-mastery warning (P43).

units.passage: They can also mislead you into thinking that you don't need to do your own reading, summary and analysis, and critical assessment of your sources.
units.why: The page warns AI tools 'can also mislead you into thinking that you don't need to do your own reading, summary and analysis'. It is a warning that AI creates a false sense that own work is unnecessary, so P43 (informs); no duty is stated that would make it P32.
units.fit_note: Stated for researchers rather than students on exams. / About AI research tools in faculty research, not student work.

units.passage: Because of the difficulty in self-determination of when GAI is facilitating-vs-hampering your own learning, the current rule in this class is to NOT allow the use Generative AI on assignments.
units.why: Gives the reason for the ban: students cannot easily judge whether AI helps or hampers their learning, a novice-judgment argument, P42. Reconciled codes: actor student, phase course-start, modality informs, type P43, unit stance neutral.
units.fit_note: Reason is that students cannot self-judge the effect on their learning. About students' inability to judge whether AI helps or hurts their learning, as the stated reason for the ban.

units.passage: If you can't complete a similar task without AI support, that's a signal to slow down and build the underlying skill.
units.why: Tells students that being unable to do the task without AI signals missing skill; a false-sense-of-mastery warning, P43.
units.fit_note: Framed as a self-check rather than a warning about exams.
